tests.title: Common.Register adds --events (default text) and --events-file flags to the shared flag set
given: a fresh flag.FlagSet with Common.Register called on it
tests.when: the --events and --events-file flags are looked up by name
then: --events exists with default value "text"
--events-file exists with default value ""
both flags sit alongside --verbose, --quiet and the other shared flags
tests.pseudocode: fs := flag.NewFlagSet("t", flag.ContinueOnError); var c Common; c.Register(fs); assert fs.Lookup("events").DefValue == "text"; assert fs.Lookup("events-file") != nil

tests.title: An invalid --events value is rejected as a usage error before any input is fetched
given: a tool invocation with --events yaml
tests.when: App.Main runs the invocation
then: the process exits with code 2
stdout carries a JSON envelope with error.stage "usage"
no HTTP fetch or model resolution occurred
zero event lines are written to stderr or an events file
tests.pseudocode: code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--events","yaml","report text"}, stdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert code == toolio.ExitUsage; var env toolio.Envelope; json.Unmarshal(stdout.Bytes(), &env); assert env.Error.Stage == "usage"; assert !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "\"type\":")

tests.title: --events-file opens the file once, truncated, flushing each JSONL line as it is written
given: a pre-existing file at the target path containing stale content
--events-file <path> passed to a tool invocation
tests.when: the run emits several events
then: the file no longer contains the stale content once opened
each emitted line is visible in the file before the run exits, not only after
every line already flushed is complete, valid JSON
tests.pseudocode: os.WriteFile(path, []byte("stale"), 0o644); go app.Main(ctx, []string{"--events-file",path,input}, ...); time.Sleep(shortDelay); lines := readLines(path); assert !strings.Contains(string(readFile(path)), "stale"); for _, l := range lines { assert json.Valid([]byte(l)) }

tests.title: --events-file carries the full JSONL stream while stderr keeps the human form under the default --events text
given: a tool invoked with --events text --events-file run.jsonl
tests.when: the run completes
then: stderr contains only human-readable [tool] lines and no JSON object
run.jsonl contains one JSON object per line covering the run's documented events
tests.pseudocode: code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--events","text","--events-file",path,input}, ...); assert !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "{\"ts\""); lines := readLines(path); for _, l := range lines { var ev map[string]any; json.Unmarshal([]byte(l), &ev) }

tests.title: --quiet suppresses stderr text under both --events values but leaves the events file intact
given: --quiet set together with --events jsonl and --events-file run.jsonl
tests.when: the run completes
then: stderr is empty
run.jsonl still contains the full event stream
tests.pseudocode: app.Main(ctx, []string{"--quiet","--events","jsonl","--events-file",path,input}, ...); assert stderr.Len() == 0; assert len(readLines(path)) > 0

tests.title: A run terminated mid-stream leaves the events file as a valid prefix with no partial line
given: --events-file <path> active and several events already flushed
tests.when: the run's context is cancelled before run_end is written, simulating a kill mid-run
then: every line already present in the file parses as complete, valid JSON
no trailing partial or corrupted line exists
the file's lines are exactly the events emitted before termination
tests.pseudocode: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); go runWithSink(ctx, path); emitN events; cancel(); lines := readLines(path); for _, l := range lines { assert json.Valid([]byte(l)) }; assert len(lines) == N

tests.title: Every emitted event carries ts, tool and type in addition to its type-specific fields
given: a JSONL sink active for a tool named "impl"
tests.when: a step event is emitted through Progress.Step
then: the decoded object has a ts field parseable as RFC3339 UTC
tool equals "impl"
type equals "step"
tests.pseudocode: p.Step("analyse","working"); line := sink.lastLine(); var obj map[string]any; json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); _, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, obj["ts"].(string)); assert err == nil; assert obj["tool"] == "impl"; assert obj["type"] == "step"

tests.title: Every event type emitted by the sink is drawn from the closed set
given: a JSONL sink active for a run exercising every event-producing call site: Step, PhaseStart/PhaseEnd, Turn, ToolCall, Check, Warn, heartbeat, run_start/run_end and Raw under --show-text
tests.when: for any sequence of Progress/Runner/Run calls made during a run
then: every decoded event's type is one of {run_start, step, phase_start, turn, tool_call, check, phase_end, warning, heartbeat, run_end, text}
tests.pseudocode: closed := map[string]bool{"run_start":true,"step":true,"phase_start":true,"turn":true,"tool_call":true,"check":true,"phase_end":true,"warning":true,"heartbeat":true,"run_end":true,"text":true}; for _, line := range capturedLines { var obj map[string]any; json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); assert closed[obj["type"].(string)] }

tests.title: Every emitted event carries only the fields documented for its own type
given: the documented per-type field table from the requirements
a run exercising every event type
tests.when: for any event emitted during that run
then: no event carries a field belonging to a type other than its own (e.g. a turn event never carries command/exit_code, a check event never carries turn/input_tokens)
tests.pseudocode: fieldsByType := map[string][]string{"turn":{"phase","turn","cost_usd","input_tokens","output_tokens"}, "check":{"command","ok","exit_code","duration_ms"}, ...}; base := []string{"ts","tool","type"}; for _, obj := range decodedEvents { allowed := append(base, fieldsByType[obj["type"]]...); for k := range obj { assert contains(allowed, k) } }

tests.title: With neither --events jsonl nor --events-file, no event objects are emitted at all
given: a tool run with the default --events text and no --events-file
tests.when: the run completes
then: stderr contains only human-readable text with no event JSON object
no events file is created or written
tests.pseudocode: app.Main(ctx, []string{input}, stdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "\"type\":"); assert !fileExists(anyEventsPath)

tests.title: Each event is serialized as one line with no embedded newline
given: a JSONL sink active
tests.when: a step event carrying a multi-line formatted message is emitted
then: the written line contains no raw newline before its own trailing line terminator
the line parses as one complete JSON object
tests.pseudocode:
p.Step("verify","line1
line2"); line := sink.lastLine(); trimmed := strings.TrimRight(line, "
"); assert !strings.Contains(trimmed, "
"); var obj map[string]any; assert json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj) == nil

tests.title: App.execute emits run_start right after the model is resolved and before the Runner is built
given: a tool invocation with --events jsonl
tests.when: App.execute reaches the point it calls e.run.SetModel and e.progress.Detail("model: …")
then: a run_start event was already written, carrying input_kind and model {spec, id, vendor}
it appears before the first phase_start event
tests.pseudocode: events := captureEvents(func(){ app.Main(ctx, []string{"--events","jsonl",input}, ...) }); assert events[0]["type"] == "run_start"; assert events[0]["input_kind"] == in.Kind.String(); assert events[0]["model"].(map[string]any)["id"] == choice.Model.ID

tests.title: App.Main emits run_end immediately before the envelope is written
given: a completed tool run with --events jsonl
tests.when: App.Main is about to call Emit(stdout, run.Envelope(...))
then: a run_end event carrying status and exit_code was written to stderr before the stdout envelope bytes
tests.pseudocode: events := captureEvents(func(){ code = app.Main(...) }); last := events[len(events)-1]; assert last["type"] == "run_end"; assert int(last["exit_code"].(float64)) == code

tests.title: Neither run_start nor run_end is emitted on -h/--help or a bare invocation
given: --events jsonl set alongside -h, and separately a bare invocation with no positional argument
tests.when: App.Main runs each of the two invocations
then: stdout carries no envelope on either path
zero event lines are written to stderr or the events file on either path
tests.pseudocode: for _, argv := range [][]string{{"--events","jsonl","-h"},{"--events","jsonl"}} { stdout.Reset(); stderr.Reset(); app.Main(ctx, argv, stdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert stdout.Len() == 0; assert countEventLines(stderr.String()) == 0 }

tests.title: run_end.status always matches the exit code that decides the envelope's own ok field
given: a family of runs producing each exit code in {ExitOK, ExitFailed, ExitUsage, ExitNeedsHuman, ExitUnverified}
tests.when: for any of these exit codes, App.Main completes a run that reaches Emit
then: the run_end event's status agrees with the envelope's ok field for every code tested
tests.pseudocode: for _, code := range []int{toolio.ExitOK, toolio.ExitFailed, toolio.ExitUsage, toolio.ExitNeedsHuman, toolio.ExitUnverified} { events, env := runProducing(code); runEnd := lastOfType(events, "run_end"); assert (runEnd["status"] == "ok") == env.OK }

tests.title: run_start is always the first event and run_end always the last, for any run that reaches Emit
given: a family of runs of varying length and outcome (success, failure, blocked) with --events jsonl active
tests.when: for any such run that reaches App.Main's Emit call
then: events[0].type == run_start for every run
events[last].type == run_end for every run
run_start appears exactly once per run
tests.pseudocode: for _, scenario := range scenarios { events := runAndCapture(scenario); assert events[0]["type"] == "run_start"; assert events[len(events)-1]["type"] == "run_end"; assert countOfType(events, "run_start") == 1 }

tests.title: Step emits a step event carrying stage and the formatted message when a JSONL sink is active
given: a Progress with an active JSONL sink
tests.when: Step("verify", "running %s", "tests") is called
then: a step event is emitted with stage "verify" and message "running tests"
tests.pseudocode: p.Step("verify", "running %s", "tests"); ev := sink.lastEvent(); assert ev["type"] == "step"; assert ev["stage"] == "verify"; assert ev["message"] == "running tests"

tests.title: Step's human-readable line stays exactly "[tool] message" with stage never shown, under any --events value
given: a Progress writing to a buffer, tested both with and without an active JSONL sink
tests.when: Step("verify", "running tests") is called in both cases
then: the human line written is exactly "[tool] running tests\n" in both cases
the word "verify" never appears in the human line
tests.pseudocode: for _, sinkActive := range []bool{true, false} { buf.Reset(); p.Step("verify","running tests"); assert buf.String() == "[tool] running tests\n" }

tests.title: Begin prints nothing and returns a no-op end function while a JSONL sink is active
given: a Progress writing to a buffer with an active JSONL sink
tests.when: Begin("checking") is called and its returned function is invoked with a summary
then: nothing is written to the buffer for the span before or after end() is called
tests.pseudocode: end := p.Begin("checking"); assert buf.Len() == 0; end("done"); assert buf.Len() == 0

tests.title: Detail never emits an event under any --events value
given: a Progress with --verbose set and an active JSONL sink
tests.when: Detail("tracing something") is called
then: no event object appears in the sink's captured stream
the existing --verbose stderr text line is still printed
tests.pseudocode: p.Detail("tracing something"); assert len(sink.events()) == 0; assert strings.Contains(buf.String(), "tracing something")

tests.title: Raw emits a text event instead of writing prose while a JSONL sink is active and --show-text is set
given: a Progress with ShowText true and an active JSONL sink, inside a known phase
tests.when: Raw("model prose") is called
then: a text event is emitted carrying phase and delta "model prose"
no raw prose bytes are written to stderr or the events file
tests.pseudocode: p.Raw("model prose"); ev := sink.lastEvent(); assert ev["type"] == "text"; assert ev["delta"] == "model prose"; assert buf.Len() == 0

tests.title: Raw does nothing when --show-text is not set, unchanged by any --events value
given: a Progress with ShowText false, tested both with and without an active JSONL sink
tests.when: Raw("model prose") is called in both cases
then: no text event is emitted in either case
no prose bytes are written to stderr or the events file in either case
tests.pseudocode: for _, sinkActive := range []bool{true, false} { p.Raw("model prose"); assert len(sink.events()) == 0; assert buf.Len() == 0 }

tests.title: Progress.Check emits a check event with the exact fields from checks.Result when a JSONL sink is active
given: a Progress with an active JSONL sink
a checks.Result{Command: "make test", OK: true, ExitCode: 0, DurationMS: 4200}
tests.when: Progress.Check(res) is called, matching how codefix.runChecks and codeimpl.runGate call it after checks.Run returns
then: a check event is emitted with command "make test", ok true, exit_code 0, duration_ms 4200
tests.pseudocode: res := checks.Result{Command:"make test", OK:true, ExitCode:0, DurationMS:4200}; p.Check(res); ev := sink.lastEvent(); assert ev["command"] == res.Command && ev["ok"] == res.OK && ev["exit_code"] == float64(res.ExitCode) && ev["duration_ms"] == float64(res.DurationMS)

tests.title: Progress.Check does nothing when no JSONL sink is active
given: a Progress with no active JSONL sink
tests.when: Progress.Check(res) is called
then: no check event is produced
no additional stderr output beyond today's Begin line is written by Check itself
tests.pseudocode: before := buf.String(); p.Check(checks.Result{Command:"make test", OK:true}); assert len(sink.events()) == 0; assert buf.String() == before

tests.title: Observer gains PhaseStart, PhaseEnd, Turn and ToolCall as additive methods that Progress implements
given: the agentrun.Observer interface and *toolio.Progress
tests.when: a *toolio.Progress value is assigned to an agentrun.Observer variable and used in agentrun.Config
then: the assignment and every existing agentrun.Config{Observer: someProgress} call site still compile unmodified
tests.pseudocode: var o agentrun.Observer = toolio.NewProgress(nil, "t", false, false); _ = agentrun.Config{Observer: o}

tests.title: Runner.Run calls Observer.PhaseStart once, before building the agent, with the phase's name, task and resolved ceilings
given: a Runner with Bounds{MaxTurns: 12, MaxBudgetUSD: 3} and a fake Observer
a Phase{Name: "implement", Task: "task-3"}
tests.when: Runner.Run(ctx, phase) is invoked
then: Observer.PhaseStart was called exactly once before any tool call, with phase "implement", task "task-3", maxTurns 12, budgetUSD 3
tests.pseudocode: runner.Run(ctx, phase); assert fakeObs.phaseStartCalls == []call{{"implement","task-3",12,3.0}}

tests.title: Runner.Run calls Observer.PhaseEnd exactly once as it returns, from the same Result it assembles
given: a Runner driving a phase to completion with a fake Observer
tests.when: Runner.Run returns Result{Turns:5, StopReason: X, Usage:{CostUSD:1.2}, Elapsed: 3s}
then: Observer.PhaseEnd was called exactly once with the phase name, stop reason, turns 5, cost 1.2 and a duration matching Elapsed
tests.pseudocode: res, _ := runner.Run(ctx, phase); assert fakeObs.phaseEndCalls == []call{{phase.Name, res.StopReason.String(), res.Turns, res.Usage.CostUSD, res.Elapsed.Milliseconds()}}

tests.title: Runner.trace calls Observer.Turn once per turn boundary with a monotonic per-phase counter, degrading to zero usage fields when the stream exposes none
given: a faux provider stream producing three turns with no dedicated per-turn usage event
a fake Observer
tests.when: Runner.Run drives the phase
then: Observer.Turn was called three times with turn numbers 1, 2, 3 in order for the same phase
each call's cost_usd, input_tokens and output_tokens are zero
tests.pseudocode: runner.Run(ctx, phase); assert fakeObs.turnCalls == []call{{phase.Name,1,0,0,0},{phase.Name,2,0,0,0},{phase.Name,3,0,0,0}}

tests.title: A traced ToolCallEndEvent calls Observer.ToolCall with blocked false when verbose tracing is on
given: a Runner with Progress.Verbose() true and a fake Observer
a phase whose stream emits a ToolCallEndEvent for tool "write_file"
tests.when: Runner.trace processes that event
then: Observer.ToolCall was called with phase, "write_file", blocked=false
tests.pseudocode: runner.traceForTest(core.ToolCallEndEvent{Block: core.ContentBlock{Name:"write_file"}}); assert fakeObs.toolCallCalls == []call{{phase.Name,"write_file",false}}

tests.title: Guard's OnBlock calls Observer.ToolCall with blocked true, correlated by tool name, alongside its existing counter and detail calls
given: a Guard configured with a read-only rule that refuses execute, verbose tracing on, and a fake Observer
tests.when: the model calls a blocked tool named "execute"
then: Observer.ToolCall was called with phase, "execute", blocked=true
the block counter was still incremented
the existing Detail line was still emitted
tests.pseudocode: decision := guardFn(ctx, blockedExecuteCallCtx); assert contains(fakeObs.toolCallCalls, call{phase.Name,"execute",true}); assert counter.count() == 1; assert len(fakeObs.detailCalls) >= 1

tests.title: agentrun.Phase carries an optional Task field, set only at codeimpl's per-task phase construction and empty elsewhere
given: codeimpl's per-task implement phase construction in codeimpl/phases.go for task "task-7"
every other pipeline's phase construction (codefix, specgen, issuetriage, and impl's other phases)
tests.when: each phase value is constructed
then: codeimpl's per-task implement Phase has Task == "task-7"
every other constructed Phase in the tree has Task == ""
tests.pseudocode: p := codeimpl.buildImplementPhase(task7); assert p.Task == "task-7"; for _, other := range otherConstructedPhases { assert other.Task == "" }

tests.title: No Observer.ToolCall call is made at all when Progress.Verbose() is false
given: a Runner with Progress.Verbose() false and a fake Observer
a phase whose stream includes both an accepted and a guard-blocked tool call
tests.when: Runner.Run drives the phase
then: Observer.ToolCall was never called
no tool_call event was ever emitted
no tool-call Detail line was printed
tests.pseudocode: runner.Run(ctx, phase); assert len(fakeObs.toolCallCalls) == 0; assert len(sink.eventsOfType("tool_call")) == 0; assert !strings.Contains(stderrBuf.String(), "→")

tests.title: toolio.Run holds a reference to the events sink, set exactly once in App.Main right after Run and Progress are constructed
given: App.Main running a tool invocation with --events jsonl
tests.when: e.run and e.progress are both constructed inside App.Main
then: the same sink instance backing e.progress is also attached to e.run before a.execute is called
the attachment happens exactly once per run
tests.pseudocode: instrumentedApp.Main(ctx, []string{"--events","jsonl",input}, ...); assert capturedRunSink == capturedProgressSink; assert attachCount == 1

tests.title: Run.Warn emits a warning event mirroring code, severity, stage and message when a sink is attached and active
given: a *Run with an attached, active JSONL sink
tests.when: Run.Warn is called recording code "comment_failed", severity "warn", stage "push", message "could not post comment"
then: a warning event is emitted with code "comment_failed", severity "warn", stage "push", message "could not post comment"
tests.pseudocode: run.Warn("comment_failed","warn","push","could not post comment"); ev := sink.lastEvent(); assert ev["type"] == "warning" && ev["code"] == "comment_failed" && ev["severity"] == "warn" && ev["stage"] == "push" && ev["message"] == "could not post comment"

tests.title: A bare Run built without an attached sink records the warning without emitting any event and does not panic
given: a *Run built with NewRun(...) and no sink attached, as today's tests already build
tests.when: Run.Warn is called
then: Run.Warnings() still returns the recorded warning
the call does not panic
no event is emitted anywhere
tests.pseudocode: run := toolio.NewRun("fix","v1"); assert !panics(func(){ run.Warn("code","warn","stage","msg") }); assert len(run.Warnings()) == 1

tests.title: For any warning recorded on a Run with an attached sink, the warning event's fields match the envelope's own warnings entry exactly
given: a *Run with an attached, active sink
tests.when: for any set of warnings recorded with varying code, severity, stage and message
then: for each recorded warning, the sink's warning event carries the identical code, severity, stage and message as the corresponding entry in run.Envelope(...).Warnings
tests.pseudocode: for _, w := range genWarnings() { run.Warn(w.code, w.severity, w.stage, w.message) }; env := run.Envelope(toolio.ExitOK, nil, nil); for i, ev := range sink.eventsOfType("warning") { assert ev["code"] == env.Warnings[i].Code && ev["message"] == env.Warnings[i].Message }

tests.title: A single heartbeat ticker runs for the run's lifetime once --events jsonl or --events-file is active
given: a run started with --events jsonl
tests.when: the run is inspected while in progress
then: exactly one heartbeat ticker is running, checking on a 1-second interval whether 15 seconds have passed since the last event
tests.pseudocode: startRunWithSink(); assert sink.activeTickerCount() == 1; assert sink.tickerInterval() == time.Second

tests.title: A heartbeat is emitted after 15 seconds of silence, carrying the last stage, elapsed_ms and accumulated cost_usd
given: a run with --events jsonl active
the last step event named stage "verify"
toolio.Run has accumulated $0.42 across its recorded phases
tests.when: 15 seconds pass with no other event emitted (using a fake clock)
then: a heartbeat event is emitted with stage "verify", an elapsed_ms approximating the run's elapsed time, and cost_usd 0.42
tests.pseudocode: fakeClock.Advance(15 * time.Second); ev := sink.lastEvent(); assert ev["type"] == "heartbeat" && ev["stage"] == "verify" && ev["cost_usd"] == 0.42

tests.title: No heartbeat appears between two events emitted less than 15 seconds apart
given: a run with --events jsonl active
a step event emitted at t=0
tests.when: a second step event is emitted 10 seconds later, using a fake clock
then: no heartbeat event appears between the two step events
the heartbeat window resets from the second step event's own timestamp
tests.pseudocode: p.Step("a","first"); fakeClock.Advance(10 * time.Second); p.Step("b","second"); assert len(sink.eventsOfType("heartbeat")) == 0

tests.title: The heartbeat ticker stops once run_end is emitted
given: a run with --events jsonl active that has just emitted run_end
tests.when: 15 more seconds pass after run_end, using a fake clock
then: no further heartbeat event is emitted
the ticker reports itself stopped
tests.pseudocode: emitRunEnd(); fakeClock.Advance(15 * time.Second); assert sink.activeTickerCount() == 0; assert len(eventsAfter(runEndIndex)) == 0

tests.title: The heartbeat's cost_usd is read from toolio.Run's existing running total, not computed a second way
given: a *Run with two phases already added via AddPhase, summing to $2.75
the heartbeat sink wired to that same Run
tests.when: a heartbeat fires
then: the heartbeat's cost_usd equals exactly the sum toolio.Run already exposes for usage.phases[]
tests.pseudocode: run.AddPhase(toolio.PhaseInfo{CostUSD:1.0}); run.AddPhase(toolio.PhaseInfo{CostUSD:1.75}); hb := triggerHeartbeat(); env := run.Envelope(toolio.ExitOK, nil, nil); assert hb["cost_usd"] == env.Usage.CostUSD

tests.title: docs/cli.md documents --events/--events-file, the ten-row type table and a worked multi-line JSONL example
given: the repository's docs/cli.md after this spec is implemented
tests.when: the file is read
then: it contains an "event types" heading
it documents both --events and --events-file
it lists all ten closed-set types
it contains a worked multi-line JSONL example

tests.title: docs/model-usage.md points at turn and phase_end as the way to watch spend live
given: the repository's docs/model-usage.md after this spec is implemented
tests.when: the file is read
then: it contains a section mentioning both the turn and phase_end event types
that section sits near the existing usage.phases[] paragraph
tests.pseudocode: text := string(readFile("docs/model-usage.md")); assert strings.Contains(text, "turn") && strings.Contains(text, "phase_end") && strings.Contains(text, "usage.phases")

tests.title: A supervisor watches a fix run live via --events jsonl and sees spend accumulate before it finishes
given: a git repository with an open GitHub issue, a scripted faux model provider, and a verification command internal/checks.Detect finds
tests.when: `fix --events jsonl <issue-url>` runs to completion
then: stderr carries a run_start event before any phase_start

a phase_end event was emitted before run_end

tests.title: A human reading stderr and a supervisor tailing a file watch the same impl run through different streams, including a heartbeat
given: a git repository with a spec package, a scripted faux provider whose phase runs long enough to cross a shortened heartbeat window, both --events text and --events-file run.jsonl given
tests.when: `impl --events text --events-file run.jsonl <spec>` runs to completion
then: stderr contains only human-readable [tool] lines, no JSON

tests.title: An invalid --events value is refused before any work happens, with no events emitted
given: a tool invocation `spec --events yaml <report>`
tests.when: the tool runs
then: the process exits with code 2
stdout carries a JSON envelope with error.stage "usage"
zero event lines were written to stderr
no fetch, model resolution or phase ran
